description: It finds the people who have an account on the site, by a search word or as a plain list: id, display name, email and the avatar address. Take it when a host names the person whose face should stand on the page, so nobody has to look up a user number. "Put my colleague on the page." The search word is part of a name or an email address, and leaving it out lists the people. It only reads and changes nothing. Read-only, it changes nothing. Data comes only from the WordPress site this chat is connected to, the site the host approved, never from another site. Without a connected site the answer says what is missing and how to connect: no numbers and no example numbers. Words hosts use: WordPress user, user id, avatar, account

limit.description: How many users to return, 1-100. Default 20.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

term.description: Part of the name or the email address. Leave it out to list the users.

name: wi_find_wordpress_user
title: Find a WordPress user as the host
